title: events/<timestamp>-<kind>.json — a fact that arose after the records were written
description:
Written once by whoever acts, and never touched again. The other records describe things that cannot change, so the few facts that appear afterwards get their own file rather than a rewrite: an original was deleted, a package was replaced, a source no longer belongs to this item.

A reader applies the events over the records: a version whose original-deleted event has fired keeps naming its original in version.json, but the file is gone and its package is from then on the only copy of the version.

File name: events/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>-<kind>.json, from this record's own at and kind — for example events/20261001T093000Z-original-deleted.json. When two events of one kind land in the same second, the writer appends the first eight characters of the eventId (…-original-deleted-1f2e3d4c.json), so no record can overwrite another.

The ids a subject names are records in this item folder: sources/<sourceId>.json, versions/<versionId>/ and the packageId of a versions/<id>/package.json.

at.description: When it happened. The file name carries the same moment, so the folder sorts in order.

by.description: The service or person that acted.

kind.description: 'original-deleted': the original file was removed from a version folder, and its package is from then on the only copy of that version. 'package-superseded': a package was replaced by one in a newer version folder; the old folder stays as it was. 'source-removed': an original that had been taken in does not belong to this item after all; its record stays, and nothing counts it any more. 'note': something a person recorded about this item that no other record holds.

sourceId.description: The source record this is about: sources/<sourceId>.json.

versionId.description: The version folder this is about: versions/<versionId>/.

packageId.description: The package this is about, by the packageId its package.json carries.

reason.description: Why it happened, in a person's words: 'space', 'replaced by a 4K master', 'wrong file'.

accepted.description: Only on original-deleted: what was accepted as lost, taken from the package's lostIfOriginalDeleted at the moment of deletion. Empty means the package carried everything the original had, and nothing was given up. It is recorded here rather than computed later, because after the deletion the original cannot be measured again.
